parts.label: (a)
parts.text: In terms of velocity and acceleration, describe uniform circular motion of an object.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Fig. 1.1 shows the view from above of a polystyrene ball undergoing horizontal circular motion of radius *R*.

[[fig:f1]]

The ball is illuminated by parallel light so that a shadow of the ball forms on a screen placed on the opposite side of the ball from the light source.

The line joining points O and P is perpendicular to the screen.

The angular speed of the circular motion is *ω*.
parts.text: State an expression, in terms of *R* and *ω*, for the speed *v* of the ball.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine an expression, in terms of *v* and *ω*, for the centripetal acceleration of the ball.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: The ball in (b) is in the position shown in Fig. 1.1, such that line OB is at an angle *θ* to the line OP.
parts.text: Determine an expression, in terms of *R* and *θ*, for the displacement *x* of the shadow from P.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The value of *θ* is zero at time *t* = 0.

State an expression for *θ* in terms of *ω* and *t*.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Use your answers in (c)(i) and (c)(ii) to show that *x* is given by

*x* = *R* sin *ωt*.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to the equation in (c)(iii), why the motion of the shadow of the ball on the screen may be modelled as simple harmonic.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.lead:
The circular motion of the ball in Fig. 1.1 has a diameter of 0.46 m and an angular speed of 1.9 rad s⁻¹.

For the simple harmonic motion of the shadow of the ball in Fig. 1.1, calculate:

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: On Fig. 1.1, draw, and label with the letter A, the position of the shadow on the screen when the shadow has its maximum positive acceleration.

figures.caption: Fig. 1.1
figures.alt: A polystyrene ball moves on a dashed circular path around O, with its shadow projected onto a screen by parallel light.
